overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating over email and in person outside an open meeting on a letter-to-the-editor and the constituent letter, though not on the letter's creation itself; ordered compliance and email release.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Board deliberated outside an open meeting in creating the May 8, 2013 letter to constituents about Town Meeting warrant articles.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board did not deliberate outside of an open meeting in connection with the creation of the May 8, 2013 letter to constituents

allegations.summary: Board members allegedly deliberated by email outside a meeting on a letter-to-the-editor and on whether to send the letter to constituents.
allegations.key_passage: the Board did improperly deliberate in creating a letter-to-the-editor upon which the May 8, 2013 letter was based, and in deciding to send the May 8, 2013 letter to constituents

allegations.summary: A member's planned in-person talk with another member and a claimed verbal go-ahead to send the letter were alleged to be off-meeting deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board has only three members, any conversation between two members concerning matters of public business within the Board's jurisdiction would be improper if conducted outside of a meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Publicly release all emails and accompanying attachments referenced in the determination, unless attorney/client privilege or a Public Records Law exemption applies, within 30 days of receipt.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law, and order the Board to publicly release all of the emails and accompanying attachments referenced in this determination, unless the attorney/client privilege or an exemption to the Public Records Law applies.
